newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile authorizes Methanex methanol plant.
newsitem.headline: Chile authorizes Methanex methanol plant.

text.p: Chile and Methanex Corp signed an investment agreement Friday authorizing the Canadian company's $375 million investment in a third methanol unit at its plant in the far south of Chile.
The agreement was signed by Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia and the general manager of Methanex Chile Ltd, Rodolfo Krause.
The plant will raise Methanex's methanol output in Chile to three million tonnes a year from two million tonnes when it comes on line in mid-1999.
"Methanex will produce six million tonnes of methanol a year, half of which will come from Chile," said Krause.
The plant will make Chile the world's largest methanol producer, said Garcia.

Methanol, a clear colorless liquid, is used as an additive in lead-free gasoline. Top markets include the United States and Europe where new environmental regulations have encouraged the switch to clean-burning methanol as a replacement for lead to cut air pollution from cars.
Methanex uses natural gas from from fields close to the border with Argentina to fuel the plant which lies on a wind-swept headland near the port of Punta Arenas,
